concepts.label: backhaul-link
concepts.gloss: A transport connection carrying traffic between a radio site and the core network, presented through the site's gateway and providing uplink service for one or more radio cells.
concepts.example: bh-441 is the site-to-core transport link presented at csg-441 and carries traffic for cells 441-A and 441-B.

concepts.label: site-gateway
concepts.gloss: The cell-site network demarcation device or logical endpoint at which a site's backhaul link is presented.
concepts.example: csg-441 terminates or presents the site-facing end of backhaul link bh-441.

concepts.label: backhaul-marking
concepts.gloss: A DiffServ QoS traffic-class marking applied to packets on a backhaul link so that the transport network can give them differentiated forwarding treatment.
concepts.example: On bh-441, latency-sensitive packets are marked EF, selected high-priority traffic is marked AF41, and ordinary traffic uses the default class.

concepts.label: backhaul-capacity
concepts.gloss: The committed traffic-carrying rate provisioned for a particular backhaul link.
concepts.example: bh-441 has a committed backhaul capacity of 8 Gbit/s for the aggregate traffic it transports.

concepts.label: backhaul-mtu
concepts.gloss: The configured maximum packet size, in octets, that a backhaul link can carry as one transport unit without requiring fragmentation.
concepts.example: With bh-441 configured to MTU 1600, it can carry packets of up to 1600 octets as single units.

concepts.label: radio-cell
concepts.gloss: A radio access service area or sector whose user and control-plane traffic is carried over an associated backhaul link.
concepts.example: Radio cells 441-A and 441-B are both served by backhaul link bh-441.

concepts.label: rrc-session
concepts.gloss: An individual Radio Resource Control connection state or session established within a specific radio cell for a device's radio signaling context.
concepts.example: rrc-session #55 is an active radio connection context associated with cell 441-A.

concepts.label: beacon-tag-7
concepts.gloss: An opaque Beacon-proprietary attribute numbered 7 that is attached to a backhaul link and whose encoded value has no defined semantics in this schema.
concepts.example: bh-441 carries beacon-tag-7 with the raw value 0x2, which is retained as a vendor-specific link attribute without interpreting what 0x2 means.
